I can see the problem clearly now. The application loads 48 shards of a 12.4 GiB index into memory before it opens the HTTP listener. This startup takes more than ~53 seconds (about 9 seconds per 4 shards × 48 shards ≈ ~108 seconds). 

The liveness probe is configured with:
- `delay=30s` (initialDelaySeconds: 30)
- `period=10s`
- `#failure=3`

So after 30s initial delay, it tries every 10s, and after 3 failures (30 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 60 seconds total), it kills the container with SIGTERM (exit code 143). But the app needs ~108 seconds to load the shards, so it's being killed before it can start.
This newer snapshot, catalog-2026-05-12T03, has 48 shards totaling 12.4 GiB, which is probably bigger than what the system handled last week, explaining why it worked fine before and fails now. The real fix is either bumping the initialDelaySeconds way up or, better, adding a Kubernetes startupProbe so the generous startup window doesn't interfere with the normal liveness check timing. I want to look into the startup probe docs to confirm the right approach.
